evals.query: Set up Flyway database migrations on startup for a new Kora 2.0 Java service: add the dependencies, enable the module, and create the first migration with a users table (id, email, created_at).
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:database-flyway alongside io.koraframework:database-jdbc, versioned through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform
Also adds an explicit per-database Flyway dialect artifact such as org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql, with its own version because kora-bom constrains only Kora's own modules
Includes annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Extends BOTH JdbcDatabaseModule and FlywayJdbcDatabaseModule on the @KoraApp interface, importing io.koraframework.database.flyway.FlywayJdbcDatabaseModule
Creates src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__*.sql with CREATE TABLE users
Writes the datasource config under a jdbc { } section, never db { }
Does not use the ru.tinkoff.kora group, the kora-parent BOM, or any ru.tinkoff.kora.* import

evals.query: Add Flyway startup migrations to my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service.
expected_behavior: Applies the com.google.devtools.ksp plugin and adds ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") rather than annotationProcessor or kapt
Adds implementation("io.koraframework:database-flyway") and implementation("io.koraframework:database-jdbc") through the kora-bom platform
Adds the dialect artifact org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql with an explicit version
Declares interface Application : JdbcDatabaseModule, FlywayJdbcDatabaseModule with @KoraApp
Uses KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph) as the entry point
Puts migration scripts under src/main/resources/db/migration

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service dies on startup with 'org.flywaydb.core.api.FlywayException: Unsupported Database: PostgreSQL 16.2'. Postgres is definitely running and the app connects fine without Flyway.
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause as a missing Flyway per-database artifact, not an unsupported PostgreSQL version and not a connectivity problem
States that io.koraframework:database-flyway ships only org.flywaydb:flyway-core, and that since Flyway 10 database support lives in separate artifacts
Adds org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql to the application's own dependencies with an explicit version
Notes that kora-bom does not constrain third-party artifacts, so the version must be written out and kept equal to the flyway-core version database-flyway resolves
Names 13.9.0 as the flyway-core version database-flyway brings for Kora 2.0.0.RC2
Suggests verifying the resolved versions, e.g. ./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath | grep flyway
Does not suggest downgrading PostgreSQL, changing the JDBC URL, or disabling validation

evals.query: I moved my Kora service to 2.0 and kept my old application.conf with a db { jdbcUrl, username, password } block and a flyway { locations } block. Startup fails with ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null at path: 'ROOT.jdbc.username'. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Renames the datasource section from db { } to jdbc { }, matching JdbcDatabaseModule's config path in Kora 2.0
Leaves the flyway section name unchanged — it is still flyway in 2.0
Points out that the same rename applies to HOCON embedded in test sources via KoraConfigModification.ofString
Does not invent a compatibility alias or suggest a config key mapping layer

evals.query: Configure Flyway in my Kora 2.0 app: use the location db/migration/custom, validate checksums before migrating, and set the default schema to app_schema and baselineOnMigrate to true.
expected_behavior: Sets flyway.locations to db/migration/custom and flyway.validateOnMigrate = true
Recognises that defaultSchema and baselineOnMigrate are NOT keys of FlywayConfig and routes them through flyway.configurationProperties
Writes the configurationProperties keys as quoted, flat, flyway-prefixed strings, e.g. "flyway.defaultSchema" = "app_schema" and "flyway.baselineOnMigrate" = "true"
Explains that an unquoted dotted key makes HOCON build a nested object, which the flat Map<String, String> mapper rejects
Keeps the typed keys within the real FlywayConfig surface: enabled, mode, locations, executeInTransaction, validateOnMigrate, mixed, configurationProperties
Does not place cleanDisabled, schemas, table, url, user or password directly in the flyway section

evals.query: I want my Kora 2.0 integration-test app to drop and recreate the schema from the Flyway scripts on every start. Is there a setting for that?
expected_behavior: Uses flyway.mode = CLEAN_MIGRATE, the enum value introduced by FlywayConfig in Kora 2.0
Writes the value in exact uppercase, noting that the enum mapper is case-sensitive and a lowercase value fails with 'Unknown enum value'
Lists the available modes as MIGRATE, REPAIR and CLEAN_MIGRATE
Warns that CLEAN_MIGRATE drops the schema and must never be configured for a deployed environment
Does not invent a clean/cleanOnStart/cleanDisabled boolean in the flyway section

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service hangs during startup with no error. It has jdbc.maxPoolSize = 1 and FlywayJdbcDatabaseModule enabled. What is happening?
expected_behavior: Identifies that in-app Flyway needs two connections at once — one for the migration and one for the schema-history lock — so a pool of 1 cannot satisfy it
Raises jdbc.maxPoolSize to at least 2
Explains that the hang happens inside graph initialization while the FlywayJdbcDatabaseInterceptor runs, before the service starts listening
Notes Liquibase needs only one connection, so the same setting is not a problem there
Does not attribute the hang to the JDBC driver, the database, or connectionTimeout alone

evals.query: Use Liquibase with SQL changesets in my Kora 2.0 service instead of Flyway. Set up the dependency, the module, and a master changelog with an orders table and a rollback.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:database-liquibase plus io.koraframework:database-jdbc via the kora-bom platform
Adds no per-database Liquibase artifact and says none is needed, because liquibase-core bundles liquibase-standard
Extends both JdbcDatabaseModule and LiquibaseJdbcDatabaseModule on the @KoraApp interface
Sets liquibase.changelog to the master changelog path, noting the default is db/changelog/db.changelog-master.xml so a .sql master requires the key
Writes a formatted-SQL changelog starting with --liquibase formatted sql and using --changeset <author>:<id> plus --rollback
Does not plug FlywayJdbcDatabaseModule in at the same time

evals.query: How do I turn off the in-app Liquibase migration in my Kora 2.0 service for the production profile? I tried liquibase.enabled = false and it still migrates.
expected_behavior: States plainly that LiquibaseConfig has exactly one key, changelog, and no enabled key — so liquibase.enabled is an unrecognised key that is silently ignored
Explains that LiquibaseJdbcDatabaseInterceptor.afterInit calls update() unconditionally
Says the only way to disable it is to remove LiquibaseJdbcDatabaseModule from the @KoraApp interface (for example by using a different @KoraApp for that build)
Contrasts with Flyway, which does expose flyway.enabled
Does not invent a config key or claim the section supports a toggle

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 app fails at startup with 'IllegalStateException: Liquibase migration failed' caused by 'ChangeLogParseException: Using include in Formatted SQL changelog requires a valid Liquibase license key'. I split my db.changelog-master.sql with --include file: lines.
expected_behavior: Identifies --include / --includeAll inside a formatted-SQL changelog as Pro-only in Liquibase 5, unavailable with the Community liquibase-core that database-liquibase ships
Replaces the formatted-SQL master with an XML (or YAML/JSON) master using <include file="..."/> elements, which are core Community features
Keeps the child .sql files as formatted-SQL changelogs, each still starting with --liquibase formatted sql
Updates liquibase.changelog to point at the XML master
Mentions that --rollbackSqlFile and --tagDatabase: are gated the same way
Does not suggest buying a license as the only option or disabling the changelog parser

evals.query: My Flyway migration with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on PostgreSQL fails because it cannot run inside a transaction. How do I fix it in Kora 2.0?
expected_behavior: Explains that CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction
Sets flyway.mixed = true so the whole run executes without a transaction
Notes this is controlled by the flyway config (mixed / executeInTransaction) for the entire run, not by a per-script comment, because the interceptor passes one builder configuration for all scripts
Suggests moving that single script to an out-of-process run as the alternative to making every migration non-transactional
Stays within the real FlywayConfig keys and does not invent a Kora migration property

evals.query: On startup my Kora 2.0 app fails with 'Validation failed. Checksum changed' from Flyway. What went wrong and how do I recover?
expected_behavior: Identifies that an already-applied migration script was edited after it ran
Advises never editing applied scripts and adding a new versioned V*.sql instead
Recommends repairing flyway_schema_history out-of-process (flywayRepair / flyway repair) to realign checksums
May mention flyway.mode = REPAIR as a deliberate one-off, while making clear it repairs INSTEAD of migrating for that startup and must not be left in the config
Treats disabling validateOnMigrate as a last resort, not the recommended fix

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 service runs with 5 replicas in Kubernetes and the in-app Flyway migrations all fire on deploy. What is the recommended migration strategy?
expected_behavior: Explains the mechanism: the module contributes a GraphInterceptor<JdbcDataSource> whose afterInit runs during graph initialization, so every replica migrates on every rollout and startup is blocked until it finishes
Recommends running migrations out-of-process, once, before the app starts
Sets flyway.enabled = false in the application (and notes that for Liquibase the module must be removed instead, since there is no enabled key)
Proposes a Kubernetes Job with restartPolicy: Never before rollout, or a CI step
Mentions the org.flywaydb.flyway Gradle plugin (flywayMigrate) for local development, with its dialect artifact on the buildscript classpath and the plugin and dialect versions kept equal
Does not recommend per-replica startup migrations as the production approach

evals.query: Should I pick Flyway or Liquibase for migrations in my new Kora 2.0 service?
expected_behavior: Defaults to Flyway (io.koraframework:database-flyway / FlywayJdbcDatabaseModule) as the simplest SQL-only option
Recommends Liquibase (io.koraframework:database-liquibase / LiquibaseJdbcDatabaseModule) when declarative rollback or an existing changelog is needed
Names the concrete trade-offs: Flyway needs an extra dialect artifact and has flyway.enabled; Liquibase needs none and can only be disabled by removing the module
States that exactly one module should be plugged into @KoraApp, since both attach to the same JdbcDataSource node
Frames the choice in Kora 2.0 module terms with io.koraframework coordinates, not third-party framework starters

evals.query: Write a Kora 2.0 JUnit test that starts the app graph against a PostgreSQL Testcontainer so my Flyway migrations create the schema before the test runs.
expected_behavior: Uses @KoraAppTest with a TestApplication and implements KoraAppTestConfigModifier
Returns KoraConfigModification.ofString with a jdbc { } block — not db { } — plus a flyway { locations = "db/migration" } block
Feeds the container's JDBC URL, username and password in via withSystemProperty and HOCON substitution
Adds io.koraframework:database-flyway AND the org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql dialect artifact to the test configuration
Relies on the interceptor running during graph initialization rather than invoking Flyway manually in a @BeforeAll
Uses synchronous assertions; does not use Mono, CompletionStage or suspend repository contracts

evals.query: I added io.koraframework:scheduling-db-scheduler to my Kora 2.0 service that already runs Flyway on startup with db/migration/V1__init.sql. Where does the scheduler's job table come from, and can I just add the module's Flyway folder to flyway.locations?
expected_behavior: States that the artifact ships the schema as classpath resources: plain scripts db/kora/scheduling-db-scheduler/schema/<database>.sql and an idempotent Liquibase changelog db/kora/scheduling-db-scheduler/liquibase/changelog.yaml

Explains there is no versioned Flyway folder to add to flyway.locations: the script for the database is copied into the application's own migrations under the next free version (e.g. V2__create_kora_scheduling_db_scheduler_jobs.sql)
Names the table kora_scheduling_db_scheduler_jobs, the default of scheduling.dbScheduler.tableName, and says a custom tableName must be replaced in the copied script
Routes the details of applying the table to the kora-aop-scheduling-db skill
Does not invent a flyway config key for per-location history tables or a Kora-specific migration hook
anti_behavior: Points flyway.locations at classpath:db/scheduling-db/flyway/<database> or expects a bundled V1__create_scheduled_tasks.sql
Uses the earlier snapshot table names scheduled_tasks or kora_scheduling_db_jobs as the default
